help_contacts.description: TWC's automated phone line for requesting payment and checking your filing date.

rules.title: Apply for unemployment benefits with TWC
rules.description: Apply with the Texas Workforce Commission (TWC) as soon as you're out of work or your hours are cut. TWC says not to apply before your last day of work. Your claim starts on the Sunday of the week you apply, and TWC only backdates a claim for good cause — so waiting can cost you weeks. You apply on TWC's own site (Unemployment Benefits Services) or by phone, not in this app. When you've applied, enter the date here.

source.title: TWC — Apply for Unemployment Benefits

additional_sources.title: TWC — Basics of Applying for Unemployment Benefits

review.notes: Claim-start and backdating wording from search summary of S18; verify exact text.

documents_needed: Your Social Security number (TWC asks for it — never enter it in this app)
Last employer's business name, address and phone number
First and last dates you worked for your last employer
Hours worked and pay rate, if you worked during the week you apply
DD Form 214 and military dates, if you served in the last 18 months
Alien Registration number, if you are not a U.S. citizen or national
questions_to_ask: Is anything missing from my application?
Which letters should I expect next, and about when?
rules.get_help: If you can't apply online or get stuck, call the TWC Tele-Center at 800-939-6631.

rules.title: Save your layoff papers as photos
rules.description: Take photos of your layoff or separation notice, final pay stub, any severance papers and any letter about your health coverage, and add them to Proof in this app. If questions come up later, having your own copies helps. The photos stay on this phone.

source.title: Texas Law Help — Unemployment Benefits Appeals in Texas

review.notes: App suggestion. Legal-aid hearing tips mention layoff notices and pay records as useful evidence.

documents_needed: Layoff or separation notice
Final pay stub
Severance papers
Health coverage letters

rules.title: Only use TWC's real website and phone numbers
rules.description: Scammers set up fake unemployment websites and send texts or e-mails with links to them. The U.S. Justice Department warns that state workforce agencies don't send texts or e-mails inviting you to apply. Type TWC's address yourself or use the official links in this app. This app will never ask for your Social Security number, passwords, PIN or bank details.

source.title: U.S. DOJ — Justice Department Warns About Fake Unemployment Benefit Websites

additional_sources.title: FTC — Scammers using fake unemployment benefits websites

review.notes: Federal guidance from 2021; still relevant but re-check for newer advisories.

rules.get_help: If you think someone filed a claim using your information, IdentityTheft.gov has federal steps to follow.

rules.title: Register on WorkInTexas.com
rules.description: TWC requires you to register for work search help on WorkInTexas.com (or at a Workforce Solutions office) within three days of applying. One TWC checklist says three business days; the app reminds you by the earlier date, three calendar days after the application date you entered.

source.title: TWC — Request Benefit Payments

additional_sources.title: TWC — Checklist: After You Apply for Unemployment Benefits

review.notes: SRD-01: '3 days' vs '3 business days' conflict. App uses calendar days (earlier).

documents_needed: A résumé or your work history (helpful for the registration)
questions_to_ask: Did my WorkInTexas registration go through?
rules.get_help: If you don't have a computer, a local Workforce Solutions office can help you register.

rules.title: Choose how TWC pays you
rules.description: Pick direct deposit or TWC's debit card in TWC's online system or by calling Tele-Serv. Do this with TWC — never enter bank or card details in this app. It doesn't need them.

source.title: TWC — Checklist: After You Apply for Unemployment Benefits

questions_to_ask: When should my first payment arrive after my first payment request?
rules.get_help: For payment method problems, call TWC Tele-Serv at 800-558-8321.

rules.title: Decide on federal tax withholding
rules.description: Unemployment benefits can be taxable. TWC's checklist asks you to decide whether you want federal income tax withheld from your payments and to fill out the form if you do.

source.title: TWC — Checklist: After You Apply for Unemployment Benefits

questions_to_ask: How do I change my tax withholding later?
rules.get_help: For tax questions about your own situation, talk to a tax professional or a free tax help program.

rules.title: Find your First Filing Date
rules.description: TWC mails "Instructions: Requesting Benefit Payments", which shows your First Filing Date and your filing day. You can also find it in TWC's online system or by calling Tele-Serv. Your first payment request is usually one to two weeks after you apply. Enter the date here so the app can remind you every two weeks.

source.title: TWC — Request Benefit Payments

documents_needed: "Instructions: Requesting Benefit Payments" letter
questions_to_ask: What is my First Filing Date and filing day?
rules.get_help: Call TWC Tele-Serv at 800-558-8321 to hear your filing date.

rules.title: Request payment (every two weeks)
rules.description: Request payment on your scheduled filing day, online in TWC's system or by phone with Tele-Serv. You'll answer questions about the last two weeks. Report all work and gross earnings for each week — even if they're more than your weekly benefit. TWC says if you don't request payment within the calendar week it's due, payment may be delayed or denied. After you submit, save the confirmation or a screenshot in Log.

source.title: TWC — Request Benefit Payments

documents_needed: Hours worked and gross earnings for each of the two weeks, if any
Your work search log for those weeks
questions_to_ask: My request says it's late — what should I do?
Why hasn't my payment arrived?
rules.get_help: If TWC's system says your payment request is late, TWC says to call the Tele-Center at 800-939-6631.

rules.title: Enter your work search requirement from TWC's letter
rules.description: TWC mails a letter with the number of work search activities you need each week and the date that starts. The number is set for your area, so it can differ from county to county. Enter both from your letter — the app won't guess.

source.title: TWC — Work Search Requirements

additional_sources.title: TWC — Required Number of Work Search Activities by County

documents_needed: TWC's work search requirements letter
questions_to_ask: How many work search activities do I need each week, and starting when?
Is my work search requirement waived?
rules.get_help: If you didn't get the letter, ask the TWC Tele-Center at 800-939-6631.

rules.title: Do and record this week's work search
rules.description: Do the number of work search activities from your TWC letter this week (Sunday–Saturday) and record each one: the date, employer and contact information, type of contact and result — the same fields as TWC's Work Search Log. Don't mail your log to TWC unless they ask. TWC can ask for any week's log, and you can lose benefits if you can't provide it. Keep it for your whole benefit year or as long as you get benefits, whichever is longer.

source.title: TWC — Work Search Requirements

review.notes: SRD-05: confirm the TWC work-search week is Sunday–Saturday.

documents_needed: Job postings or applications you used
Names and contact info of employers you contacted
questions_to_ask: Does this activity count as a work search activity?
rules.get_help: Your local Workforce Solutions office can explain what counts as a work search activity in your area.

rules.title: Stay able and available for full-time work
rules.description: TWC's checklist says that while you get benefits you must be physically and mentally able to work and available to accept a suitable job right away. If something changes (illness, travel, school, childcare), ask TWC how it affects your claim.

source.title: TWC — Checklist: After You Apply for Unemployment Benefits

questions_to_ask: How does this change in my situation affect my claim?
rules.get_help: Only TWC can decide how a change affects your claim. Ask the Tele-Center at 800-939-6631.

rules.title: Skim TWC's Unemployment Benefits Handbook
rules.description: TWC's checklist asks you to review the Unemployment Benefits Handbook it sends you. It's the official rulebook for your claim — this app only organizes steps from it and other TWC pages.

source.title: TWC — Unemployment Benefits Handbook

review.notes: Confirm handbook URL is the current edition.

rules.get_help: If the handbook and this app ever disagree, the handbook and your letters win.

rules.title: If you start working again, report it
rules.description: If you work while requesting benefits — even part-time — TWC requires you to report your hours and gross earnings for each week you request payment. Not reporting earnings accurately can be treated as fraud.

source.title: TWC — Report Your Work & Earnings

documents_needed: Pay stubs from any new work
questions_to_ask: I started a new job — do I keep requesting payment for the last weeks?
rules.get_help: Ask TWC how to report your first weeks back at work: Tele-Center 800-939-6631.

rules.title: Health coverage: 60-day Marketplace window
rules.description: Losing job-based health coverage lets you sign up for a plan on HealthCare.gov during a 60-day Special Enrollment Period. The app counts 60 days from the coverage end date you entered. HealthCare.gov decides your exact window — check it there.

source.title: HealthCare.gov — If you lose job-based health insurance

review.notes: Texas uses HealthCare.gov (federal Marketplace) — confirm for 2027 plan year.

documents_needed: Letter or notice showing when your coverage ends
Household income estimate
questions_to_ask: What date does HealthCare.gov use as my coverage loss date?
rules.get_help: HealthCare.gov and free local assisters can help you compare options. The app can't tell you which plan to pick.

rules.title: COBRA: note your election deadline
rules.description: COBRA lets you pay to keep your job-based health plan for a limited time. The U.S. Department of Labor says you have 60 days to elect, counted from the later of when coverage ends or when the notice is given. Your notice shows the deadline — that date wins. Without it, the app estimates 60 days from the mailing date.

source.title: U.S. DOL — FAQs on COBRA Continuation Health Coverage for Workers

documents_needed: COBRA election notice
questions_to_ask: What will COBRA cost per month?
When is my first premium due after I elect?
rules.get_help: The plan administrator named on the notice answers COBRA questions. The U.S. Department of Labor's benefits advisors can also help.

rules.title: Verify your identity for TWC
rules.description: If TWC sends you a letter asking you to verify your identity, follow its link or instructions. TWC offers two ways: online with ID.me, or in person at a participating U.S. Post Office. TWC says not completing it delays or denies benefits. Only use the link printed on the TWC letter or TWC's website.

source.title: TWC — Identity Verification

additional_sources.title: TWC — In-person identity verification at USPS

review.notes: No standard deadline found; relies on the date printed on the letter.

documents_needed: The TWC letter
A government-issued photo ID
questions_to_ask: Did TWC receive my identity verification?
rules.get_help: If ID.me doesn't work for you, ask TWC about in-person verification at a post office: Tele-Center 800-939-6631.

rules.title: Check your Statement of Wages
rules.description: Compare the employers and wages on the statement with your own pay records. If something is missing or wrong, TWC says to call the Tele-Center right away. If you disagree with TWC's corrected wages, appeal instructions are on the statement. Without a printed date, the app reminds you 14 days after the mailing date, the usual TWC appeal window — the statement's own instructions win.

source.title: TWC — Learning the Result of Your Application for Benefits

review.notes: SRD-06: 14-day window for wage statement appeals is low-confidence; verify.

documents_needed: Pay stubs or W-2s for the past 18 months
The Statement of Wages
questions_to_ask: An employer or wages are missing from my statement — how do I fix it?
rules.get_help: Call the TWC Tele-Center at 800-939-6631 about mistakes. For disputes, Texas Law Help and legal aid can advise.

rules.title: Read your determination and note the appeal deadline
rules.description: A determination is TWC's decision on your claim or an issue in it. If you disagree, TWC says an appeal must be in writing and filed within 14 days of the date the notice was mailed; the last day is printed on the form. You can appeal online, by mail, by fax or in person at Workforce Solutions — not by phone or e-mail. This app can't tell you whether to appeal. If you're unsure, contact legal aid well before the deadline.

source.title: TWC — Introduction to the Unemployment Benefits Appeal Process

additional_sources.title: Texas Law Help — Unemployment Benefits Appeals in Texas

review.notes: SRD-02: 'from mailing' vs 'of receiving' conflict; app uses mailing date (earlier). SRD-03: holiday extension not applied (conservative).

documents_needed: The determination letter
Anything that supports your side (e.g. layoff notice, pay records, messages with your employer)
questions_to_ask: What facts was this decision based on?
If I appeal, what documents should I send and where?
Do I keep requesting payment while an appeal is pending?
rules.get_help: Whether to appeal is your decision. Texas Law Help and legal aid (such as TRLA) can advise — contact them early. TWC's Tele-Center (800-939-6631) can explain the letter.

rules.title: Get ready for your telephone hearing
rules.description: TWC mails a hearing packet about 5 to 10 days before the hearing. It includes the date, time and number to call, instructions for sending documents before the hearing, and the information TWC gathered. Follow the packet's instructions for documents, and be ready on time with your documents and any witnesses. The hearing is usually your one chance to tell your side.

source.title: TWC — Introduction to the Unemployment Benefits Appeal Process

additional_sources.title: Texas Law Help — Unemployment Benefits Appeals in Texas

review.notes: Packet timing from legal-aid summary; verify on TWC page.

documents_needed: The hearing packet
Your documents, sent the way the packet says
Names and phone numbers of any witnesses
questions_to_ask: How and by when do I send documents for my hearing?
What happens if my phone drops during the hearing?
rules.get_help: Legal aid may be able to represent or coach you. Contact them as soon as you get the hearing notice.

rules.title: Hearing decision: note the Commission appeal deadline
rules.description: If you disagree with the hearing (Appeal Tribunal) decision, you can appeal to the Commission in writing within 14 days of the date the decision was mailed. The deadline is printed on the decision. This app can't tell you whether to appeal.

source.title: TWC — Introduction to the Unemployment Benefits Appeal Process

additional_sources.title: Texas Law Help — Unemployment Benefits Appeals in Texas

documents_needed: The hearing decision
questions_to_ask: How do I send an appeal to the Commission?
rules.get_help: Whether to appeal is your decision. Legal aid can advise — contact them right away because the window is short.

rules.title: RESEA: watch the orientation and attend your appointment
rules.description: If TWC selects you for RESEA (Reemployment Services and Eligibility Assessment), participation is mandatory. Watch the RESEA orientation video in WorkInTexas.com and attend the one-on-one appointment on your letter with a Workforce Solutions specialist. Missing it repeatedly can suspend your benefits until you take part.

source.title: TWC — Reemployment Services & Eligibility Assessment

review.notes: RESEA rules changing under HB 3698 (2025); re-check after Chapter 815 rules are adopted.

documents_needed: The RESEA letter
Your résumé and work search log
questions_to_ask: Can I reschedule my RESEA appointment?
rules.get_help: Call the Workforce Solutions office on your letter if you can't make the appointment.

rules.title: Respond to TWC's request
rules.description: TWC's checklist says to respond when TWC or your local Workforce Solutions office contacts you — for example, to call the Tele-Center or report to an office. Respond by the date on the letter. Keep a note of when you called and who you spoke with in Log.

source.title: TWC — Checklist: After You Apply for Unemployment Benefits

documents_needed: The letter or message
questions_to_ask: What exactly do you need from me, and by when?
rules.get_help: TWC Tele-Center: 800-939-6631.

rules.title: Read the letter and note any date on it
rules.description: You logged a letter. Read it for anything you need to do and any date. If it has a deadline, enter it so the app can remind you. If you don't understand it, add a question to your list for TWC.
questions_to_ask: What does this letter mean for my claim?
